taylor: FYI perf alert from staging for model-onboard v2. Throughput dropped ~35% after the tokenizer/config bump that merged last night.
samir: saw the CI perf job fail too, job: `perf/staging/throughput-64` — p50 went 28ms -> 110ms, and token/sec down 37%.
perf-ci-bot: [perf/staging/throughput-64] failure: throughput_regression >= 20% (baseline 12200 tok/s, current 7600 tok/s)
maria: initial profiling suggests more small/long sequence mixes now (tokenizer splits changed). Batching heuristic is grouping by avg_len and routing to fused_attention_v2 vs generic kernels — seems misrouted.
taylor: here's the quick trace from runtime profiler (trimmed):
```
Kernel chosen: generic_attention
avg_seq_len: 42
p50_infer_ms: 115
KV hit rate: 82%
Batch size: 12
```
samir: before bump we were picking `fused_attention_v2` for these shapes. New tokenizer produces many short prefixes then long tails, confusing the seq_len histogram used by kernel selector.
david: I ran a git bisect locally. Culprit commit: abcdef12cd34 — "tokenizer: preserve-zero-width-chars in split". It changes the token length distribution for our benchmark prompts.
maria: confirmation: bisect -> abcdef12cd34. Reverting locally restores perf to baseline.
taylor: can we avoid full revert? Maybe adjust kernel-selection policy to use max_seq_in_batch or seq_len_stddev rather than avg? Current heuristic:
```
if avg_seq_len < 64 -> use fused_attention_v2
else -> use generic_attention
```
That avg is brittle when distribution is bimodal.
samir: proposed short-term fix: add fallback: if seq_len_stddev > 40 -> prefer fused_attention_v2. Patch ready, running internal perf sweep.
perf-ci-bot: running perf/smoke/kernel-selector-sweep
maria: also KV cache behavior: because tokenizer added invisible chars, prefixes are slightly different so prefix-KV cache hit rate dropped for the first 2 tokens, causing cache churn. KV hit drop from 91% -> 78% on sampled traces.
david: patch idea B: normalize tokenizer output for inference (strip zero-width) when `inference_mode=true`. Cheaper than changing kernels. But risky for text fidelity.
taylor: agree with staged approach: 1) apply kernel-selector fallback (low risk) 2) run perf CI sweep 3) if still regressions, consider tokenizer inference-normalize or revert tokenizer PR.
samir: I pushed PR: https://git.redwood/infra/+/pull/789/fallback-kernel-seqstd
maria: running internal smoke: throughput back to 11800 tok/s, p50 34ms on staging with patch applied (preliminary).
perf-ci-bot: [perf/smoke/kernel-selector-sweep] success: regression mitigated on staging snapshot.
taylor: assign remediation tasks: @samir follow-up with QA for canary; @maria run longer-load test; @david coordinate with model-onboard team about tokenizer change rollback options.
david: noted, I'll ping the model-onboard PR author and schedule a quick sync.
taylor: leaving this here — if CI sweep stays green we'll do a small canary deploy and monitor KV hit metrics + p50. :eyes:
samir: thanks all. I'll post results in #eng-runtime once canary starts.
maria: adding perf graphs to the ticket: infra/issue/INC-6242
perf-ci-bot: ticket INC-6242 linked to thread.
